In this piece, I will argue that fossil fuels, often vilified as the primary cause of climate change, may actually be an unlikely hero for the environment.

In many parts of the world, access to electricity is still a luxury, and fossil fuels have played a crucial role in expanding access to this essential resource. In fact, according to the International Energy Agency, fossil fuels currently account for over 80% of global electricity generation, and are responsible for powering everything from homes and businesses to hospitals and schools.

Another argument in favor of fossil fuels is that they have enabled economic growth and development in many parts of the world. Unlike fossil fuels, which can be burned on demand, renewable energy sources such as solar and wind are dependent on weather conditions and can be unpredictable. This can make it difficult to ensure a reliable and consistent supply of energy, and can lead to higher costs and greater complexity in the energy system.

Another challenge is the issue of energy storage. While renewable energy sources can generate electricity, they cannot store it for later use. This means that any excess energy generated must be either wasted or used immediately, which can lead to inefficiencies and higher costs.
